answer: Trust an identity only when several independent issuers each vouch for a different fact — one checks a device, one a payment history, one a community record — and no one issuer can mint an agent alone. A farmer can buy one corrupt attester, but each fake still needs the whole quorum, so forging a thousand identities means bribing a thousand sets, and cost multiplies per clone. A fable of cheap clones collapses when the prism of separate checks splits one lie into many visible failures. Limits: issuers can collude, and people who wander outside formal systems may lack attestations.
